head_commit.message:
build(sdk): remove the drifting vendored Go/Rust SDK copies; test the pinned standalone SDKs

sdk/go and sdk/rust were second copies of github.com/Actenon/sdk-go and
github.com/Actenon/sdk-rust. sdk/go even declared the standalone module path
(github.com/actenon/sdk-go), so nobody could depend on the kernel copy, yet
canonical.go/verifier.go and canonical.rs/verifier.rs had diverged from the
standalone SDKs users actually install. The kernel's CI tested the copies,
not the SDKs, and the Rust copy's Clippy step was red on PR #37.

Now the kernel's CI checks out each standalone SDK at the commit pinned in
sdk/standalone-sdk-pins.json and:
- requires its vendored kernel vectors to be byte-identical to this tree
  (scripts/check_standalone_sdk_fixtures.py: the vector-lock copy and every
  KERNEL_UNLOCKED file), and
- runs its full test suite with ACTENON_KERNEL_VECTOR_LOCK pointing at this
  tree's conformance/vector-lock.json.
Each SDK already checks the reverse direction against its KERNEL_PIN, so a
vector change on either side fails CI until the other follows.
scripts/verify_sdk_conformance.sh does the same locally (.sdk-cache/).
Docs and conformance/suite.json point at the standalone repositories.

Verified: check script passes for sdk-go@37700d0 and sdk-rust@261ffbf and
fails on an injected change to a locked and to an unlocked fixture;
verify_sdk_conformance.sh passes; kernel pytest 710 passed, 3 skipped.

actenon-mcp --demo, actenon-kernel conformance run), the named unsafe
overrides, and production configs with ACTENON_REPLAY_DB or a shared store.

head_commit.message:
fix(schemas): accept the canonicalization labels the verifier accepts

Six published schemas pinned `canonicalization` to the legacy constant
"RFC8785-JCS", while the kernel mints every new artefact with
ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1 (CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE) and its verifier accepts
both (ACCEPTED_CANONICALIZATION_PROFILES). Every freshly minted PCCB,
receipt/refusal correlation digest, approval, countersignature and
transparency digest therefore failed the kernel's own schema.

The schemas now allow exactly the accepted set. A new test walks every
schema and asserts each canonicalization constraint equals the
verifier's accepted profiles, so a schema can drift from the verifier
in neither direction.

fix(canonical): typed error for lone surrogates, plain ints for IntEnum, drop rejected label

Three protocol-alignment fixes (reported by the protocol audit):

- A string containing a lone surrogate reached .encode("utf-8") and
  raised UnicodeEncodeError. It is now refused as the protocol's typed
  CanonicalisationError (still a ValueError, so every existing
  fail-closed handler catches it).
- Integers were serialised with str(), which on Python 3.10 renders an
  IntEnum as "HTTPStatus.OK" instead of "200". int.__repr__ is used now.
- local_runtime's broker-demo placeholder PCCB declared the
  canonicalization label "actenon-jcs-sha256-v1", which the protocol
  explicitly rejects; it now uses the kernel's CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE.

Valid input is byte-identical: new tests pin equality with the protocol
reference, and a 20,000-input differential run (nested objects, arrays,
big ints, control chars, astral/BMP-private keys) matched exactly.

head_commit.message:
fix(cli): verify-receipt/refusal stop saying "verified" for unchecked artifacts; verify-proof --public-key-jwk (F10)

`verify-receipt --receipt X` printed "Receipt verified." after only
parsing X: a v1 Receipt carries no signature, and with no linked
artifact nothing is compared, so a fabricated or tampered receipt
"verified" (E2E F10). Same for verify-refusal.

Now:
- with no linked artifact the command exits 1 with "Receipt NOT
  verified: only its structure was checked"; --structure-only makes a
  shape check explicit and still says NOT verified.
- with links it prints "Receipt links verified.", what it was checked
  against, verifies the linked PCCB's signature when a verifier is
  available (local key or --public-key-jwk) and fails if it does not
  verify, and states that the receipt itself is unsigned (pointing at
  the attestation commands).

`verify-proof` only knew the public local HMAC key, so Ed25519 proofs
(what actenon-permit mints) failed with "no local verifier". New
